---
title: "Name the Fears"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** none. **Objective:** name what worries you about large language model (LLM) agents (an agent is a model running inside a program that picks and runs tools in a loop toward a goal), and learn the habit that answers each worry.
**Time:** about 10 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim: nothing here depends on a tool version.</span>
:::

## Why start with fears

You do not have to like these tools. Many careful people in science are wary of them, and most of the wariness is reasonable.
This odyssey keeps your worries and gives each one a **habit** that makes the risk smaller, so you can decide with your eyes open.

Each worry below is a real enemy in this land. Each has a counter-habit, and the rest of the odyssey trains them.

| The worry | The enemy | The counter-habit | Where you learn it |
|---|---|---|---|
| "It will stop me learning." | Learning-drain | Write it first, predict before you look, ask it to explain while you do the work. | Biodiversity Reef |
| "It produces slop in bulk." | Slop-ooze | Small steps, tests before code, a review budget. | Sequence Maze |
| "It makes things up." | Mirage | Check against something the agent did not write. | Sequence Maze |
| "Someone else has to review all this." | Review-leech | Review it yourself first, say that you used an LLM, send small changes. | Biodiversity Reef |
| "It could delete my work or leak my data." | Data-wipe | Undo (git), permissions, a sandbox (an operating-system layer that limits what commands can touch) or scratch directory, no secrets in prompts (a prompt is the text you send to the model). | Ancient DNA Crypt |
| "I do not understand what it did." | Black-box husk | Ask for a changelog and explain it back before you keep it. | Sequence Maze |
| "Finishing this with an agent will feel hollow, as if it was not really my work." | Hollow-victory | Make the decisions, be able to explain each step, keep a short decision log, credit the agent's part openly. | Biodiversity Reef |
| "Everyone will expect work to be done faster now." | Clock-shifter | Say where the time goes, agree timelines that include review, share how long checking took. | Biodiversity Reef |

*Slop* is low-quality bulk output. A *review budget* means you only produce as much as you can honestly review today.

::: {.callout-note}
Sometimes the right answer is to skip the LLM. Part of the skill is knowing when.
:::

## Battle: name the counter-habit

<div data-ao-test="basecamp-name-the-fears" data-xp="40"></div>

::: {.ao-lore}
## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Reduce hallucinations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it lists concrete habits such as allowing "I don't know" and checking claims against quotes, and says plainly that none of them remove errors.
- [Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13548): Sharma et al. (Anthropic authors), ICLR 2024, paper. Why read: it shows assistants often agree with a user's stated view, so you can see why asking for the case against your idea helps.
- [Mitigating prompt injections in browser use](https://www.anthropic.com/research/prompt-injection-defenses): Anthropic, article. Why read: a vendor's own account that injection is not solved and what defences exist; the attack figures are Anthropic's own tests.
- [Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it describes the built-in protections and advice on untrusted content, a practical start for the fear of prompt injection.
:::
